title: Reading Test 3: Rooftop Gardens in Modern Cities

passage.label: A
passage.text: Rooftop gardens are becoming more common in dense cities where ground-level space is limited. These gardens can be installed on residential buildings, offices, schools, and public facilities. Some are designed mainly for relaxation, while others are used to grow vegetables or support urban wildlife.

passage.label: B
passage.text: One advantage of rooftop planting is temperature control. Soil and vegetation can absorb sunlight and reduce the amount of heat transferred into a building. This may lower the need for air conditioning in summer, especially in poorly insulated buildings.

passage.label: C
passage.text: Rooftop gardens can also help manage rainwater. During heavy rainfall, plants and soil hold part of the water temporarily, slowing the speed at which it enters drainage systems. This does not remove the need for proper drains, but it can reduce pressure during storms.

passage.label: D
passage.text: Despite these benefits, rooftop gardens require careful planning. Engineers must check whether a roof can support the extra weight of soil, water, plants, and people. Maintenance is also important because neglected gardens can become unsafe or fail to survive dry periods.

passage.label: E
passage.text: Successful projects often involve cooperation between architects, residents, building managers, and local authorities. When these groups work together, rooftop gardens can provide environmental benefits as well as pleasant shared spaces above the busy streets below.
